evidence: Receiving P assay t=48h = 2.94 g/L vs source-1/2/3 = 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L (available at 52h)
Receiving DO2 at 52.0h = 9.92 mg/L, well above 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving DO2/P profiles match source batches phase-for-phase (lag ~24h, ramp after 30h)
args.rationale: Receiving fermentation is performing equivalently to all three source batches at the 52 h decision point: delayed P assay at t=48 h is 2.94 g/L (source batches 2.98-3.06 g/L), indicating no production deficit. DO2 is ~9.9-10 mg/L at 52 h, far above the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint, and follows the same sawtooth trajectory (periodic dips to ~7-8 mg/L around 24-28 h with aeration resets) seen in the sources. No evidence of underperformance or oxygen-limitation risk; altering feed or air would deviate from the calibrated process without justification. Normal case: recommend KEEP.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and may not reflect hidden receiving parameters, but the strong one-to-one agreement in both DO2 and P trajectories across three source batches gives high confidence. Residual risk: a divergence could emerge after 52 h (as sources show product plateau/decline after ~76 h), but interventions available (feed reduction, air increase) do not plausibly improve late-stage product mass retention without cost.
